messages:
opsbot: Pager P1: elevated error and tail-latency observed across inference-prod-apac and inference-prod-eu at 2024-06-27 09:00 UTC. Paging eng-sre oncall.
maria: seeing repeated 429 + connection resets on apac-edge. p95 jumping ~800ms, p99 > 2s. Some pools at capacity; queues growing.
samir: pulling smart-routing metrics now. Could be a single-tenant blast or a multi-tenant burst?
carmen: flow logs show a handful of org_ids spiking concurrency to hundreds of parallel streams from ap-southeast-1. Also a surge of long-lived streaming sessions.
maria: hypothesis: a misconfigured customer job plus steady free-tier bots. plan: quick tenant-level burst tokens + tighten baseline trial bucket, plus short steering to eu for non-latency-sensitive routes.
samir: agree. sequence: 1) apply per-org burst cap to suspicious orgs, 2) reduce free/trial bucket in apac, 3) add steering policy that routes low-priority generation to eu-fallback with progressive weights, 4) disable long streaming on baseline routes for immediate relief. Keep changes reversible.
maria: applying tenant caps (hotpatch) for two orgs identified: org_8932, org_7744
```
redwoodctl tenants update --org org_8932 --set "burst_tokens=50,concurrent_streams=20" --reason "emergency surge apac"
redwoodctl tenants update --org org_7744 --set "burst_tokens=50,concurrent_streams=20" --reason "emergency surge apac"
```
dev-bot: tenant update success: org_8932, org_7744 (ver=20240627-tt1)
maria: lowering trial/free bucket in ap-southeast: 30rpm -> 10rpm
```
redwoodctl policies patch --region ap-southeast --policy trial-bucket --set "requests_per_minute=10" --note "emergency apac throttle"
```
opsbot: policy applied trial-bucket ap-southeast (ver=20240627-rl2) by maria
samir: adding steering rule: non-critical text-gen routes -> eu-west fallback with initial weight 25%. will monitor q length and error rates before ramp
```
redwoodctl routing create --from-region ap-southeast --to-region eu-west --routes "text.generate.low,embeddings.batch.low" --weight 25 --auto-ramp=false
```
dev-bot: routing rule created id rt-b1a (author=maria)
maria: toggling streaming off for baseline-v2 at 10% rollout to kill long-lived connections and free ephemeral kernels. This will impact apps that rely on chunked streams briefly.
```
redwoodctl feature toggle --target baseline-v2 --feature streaming --state off --rollout 10
```
opsbot: feature toggle queued baseline-v2 streaming off (rollout=10%)
carmen: immediate signal: queue depth falling from 6k -> 2.4k in 8 mins. 5xx placings down by half. Good short-term effect.
samir: logs show one org still racing requests; maintaining its cap but needs customer outreach.
maria: draft customer note for org_8932: "We applied emergency rate controls on your tenant due to unusually high concurrent traffic causing platform instability in APAC. Please contact SE to coordinate backfill/optimized client config." Approve?
jonah: +1 send via support immediately. Also recommend we enable automated hotspot detector to surface tenant spikes earlier.
maria: telemetry update: p95 overall back to ~300ms, p99 ~1.1s, 429 down to 0.6% from 3.8%. streaming disconnects reported ~120 sessions in apac.
samir: next mitigation if not stable: global low-priority token bucket and quantized fallback for high-cost lanes (small-quant8). We prefer not to evict customers but we can reroute and serve a lighter variant.
maria: executed a canary switch: low-priority routes now prefer small-quant8 in apac for 15% of traffic
```
redwoodctl model serve --model small-quant8 --route-type low-priority --region ap-southeast --weight 15
```
dev-bot: model variant routing updated (ver=20240627-mv1)
carmen: monitoring shows per-token cost drop and slight tail-latency increase on canary as expected, but overall queue relief continues.

maria: setting incident timer 45 minutes. if queue >3k or 5xx >1% after that, we escalate to capacity add and consider a temporary global throttle for anonymous/trial traffic.

samir: leaving runbook snippets and commands used in thread for handoff.
- redwoodctl tenants update --org org_8932 --set "burst_tokens=50,concurrent_streams=20"
- redwoodctl policies patch --region ap-southeast --policy trial-bucket --set "requests_per_minute=10"
- redwoodctl routing create --from-region ap-southeast --to-region eu-west --routes "text.generate.low,embeddings.batch.low" --weight 25
- redwoodctl feature toggle --target baseline-v2 --feature streaming --state off --rollout 10
- redwoodctl model serve --model small-quant8 --route-type low-priority --region ap-southeast --weight 15

maria: handing off to night oncall jonah in 12 minutes. leaving suggested watchlist: queue_depth.ap-southeast, 5xx.rate, 429.rate, per-org concurrency org_8932/org_7744. If regress, revert streaming toggle and increase steering weight to 40%.
jonah: ack, taking over monitoring. will keep tenant caps in place and steering at 25% ramp. I'll coordinate with support on org outreach and will escalate to infra if any pool hits 95% kernel utilization again.
maria: incident summary for postmortem: root cause: concentrated high-concurrency tenants + long-lived streaming sessions saturating APAC high-tier pools; mitigations: tenant caps, trial bucket tightening, regional steering to EU fallback, streaming partial disable, quantized fallback canary. impact: transient streaming interruptions for some APAC users and elevated tail latency for ~20 minutes. action items: tenant spike detector, per-tenant SLA guardrails, auto-fallback policy for model variants, clearer customer guidance for streaming best-practices.
opsbot: Incident P1 mitigations applied. Handoff complete. Thread archived at 2024-06-27 09:30 UTC.
